The test image shows a soybean stem split open lengthwise. The internal pith appears light gray/white with what may be small dark specks. The stem is dry and mature. This is a **stem** image.

Top candidates from the stem list: Charcoal_Rot, Brown_Stem_Rot, White_Mold, Fusarium, Phytophthora. Let me compare reference images one at a time.
Charcoal rot reference shows a gray, dry stem with external discoloration. Similar dry appearance to the test image. Now let me check Brown_Stem_Rot.
Brown stem rot shows green stems with brown internal pith. Very different from the dry, mature test image. Let me check White_Mold.
White mold shows bleached stems with fluffy white growth and external black sclerotia. Doesn't match the test image. Let me check Fusarium and Phytophthora.
Fusarium shows young green stems with brown vascular tissue. Very different from the test image. Let me check Phytophthora and the second Charcoal_Rot stem reference.
Phytophthora shows dark brown stem lesions on living plants. Not matching. Let me check the second Charcoal_Rot stem image.

This Charcoal_Rot reference is very similar to the test image - dry, mature stem split lengthwise with light gray internal tissue and dark specks on the surface. Strong match. Let me use my remaining 2 views on Anthracnose and Rhizoctonia stems.
Anthracnose shows dark lesions with black fruiting bodies on stems. Doesn't match. Last view on White_Mold's other stem reference.

White Mold shows bleached stems with dark lesions at nodes. Doesn't match.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a dry, mature soybean stem split lengthwise with:
- Light gray/whitish internal pith tissue
- Gray streaking visible internally
- Dry, weathered exterior with possible small dark specks

The strongest match is **Charcoal_Rot** (reference Dise_49 was nearly identical): dry stem split open showing light gray internal tissue with gray streaking and small dark microsclerotia. The symptom description matches perfectly: "light gray streaks and small black specks (microsclerotia) beneath the epidermis giving a charcoal-sprinkled appearance, with reddish-brown discoloration in the pith and vascular tissues."

Other candidates eliminated:
- Brown_Stem_Rot: would show distinctly brown pith (not gray/white)
- White_Mold: would show fluffy white growth and large black sclerotia
- Fusarium/Phytophthora: affect younger, green plants differently
- Anthracnose: shows dark irregular lesions with black fruiting bodies
